findings.title: Duplicated _buildOptions / _buildDefaultOptions / _buildLzReceiveOptions across 5 contracts
findings.description: The identical LZ options builder function is copy-pasted across 5 contracts under different names: CreditManager._buildLzReceiveOptions (L319), CrossChainAssetController._buildOptions (L351), PPTOFTAdapter._buildDefaultOptions (L299), PPTOFT._buildDefaultOptions (L298), PPTSatellite._buildDefaultOptions (L324), and RemoteAssetAdapter._buildOptions (L280). Meanwhile, LzOptionsLib already exists as a shared library that provides exactly this functionality but is never imported or used by any of these contracts.

findings.title: Duplicated error definitions across contracts instead of using shared LayerZeroErrors library
findings.description: LayerZeroErrors.sol defines 11 shared error types, but every contract redeclares its own copies: InvalidAmount (CreditManager L16, CrossChainAssetController L105, PPTOFTAdapter L99, PPTOFT L76, PPTSatellite L73, LiquidityPool L36, RemoteAssetAdapter implicit), UnknownMessageType (CreditManager L25, CrossChainAssetController L112, PPTSatellite L80, RemoteAssetAdapter L69), ZeroAddress (PPTOFTAdapter L105, LiquidityPool L41, RemoteAssetAdapter L70), UnauthorizedSource (CreditManager L26, CrossChainAssetController L111). The LayerZeroErrors library is never imported anywhere.

findings.title: Near-duplicate _debitView, _removeDust, _buildSendMessage, _bytes32ToAddress between PPTOFT and PPTOFTAdapter
findings.description: PPTOFT and PPTOFTAdapter share 4 identical internal functions: _debitView (PPTOFT L256-268, PPTOFTAdapter L264-276), _removeDust (PPTOFT L282-284, PPTOFTAdapter L289-291), _buildSendMessage (PPTOFT L287-289, PPTOFTAdapter L294-296), and _bytes32ToAddress (PPTOFT L304-306, PPTOFTAdapter L304-306). These are line-for-line identical implementations. Since both handle OFT mechanics, extracting to a shared base contract or library would eliminate 4 duplicate functions (~30 lines).

findings.title: CreditManager.rebalance has high cyclomatic complexity with nested branching in a loop
findings.description: The rebalance function (L139-186, 48 lines) has a cyclomatic complexity of approximately 8 (2 guard clauses + loop + 3 branches inside loop + 1 ternary). It mixes validation, state updates, cross-chain message construction, fee splitting, and event emission in one function body. The inner loop body alone spans ~30 lines with 3 levels of nesting (function > loop > if/else if). This makes it the most complex function in the codebase.

findings.title: Near-duplicate _sendWithdrawConfirmation and _sendYieldReport in RemoteAssetAdapter
findings.description: The functions _sendWithdrawConfirmation (L202-221) and _sendYieldReport (L225-243) are structurally identical: build payload with a message type and amount, build options, quote fee, check balance, send if sufficient. The only differences are the message type constant, the event emitted, and the parameter name. This is a textbook case for extracting a shared helper.

findings.title: Duplicated removeChain/removeSupportedChain array-removal pattern across CreditManager and CrossChainAssetController
findings.description: The swap-and-pop array removal pattern is duplicated identically in CreditManager.removeChain (L236-242) and CrossChainAssetController.removeSupportedChain (L309-315). Both operate on _supportedChains arrays of type uint32[]. This is a common utility pattern that could be extracted to a shared library function.

findings.title: Duplicate struct definitions (SendParam, MessagingFee, MessagingReceipt, OFTReceipt) in IPPTOFT and IPPTOFTAdapter
findings.description: IPPTOFT (L14-42) and IPPTOFTAdapter (L11-38) define identical structs: SendParam (7 fields), MessagingFee (2 fields), MessagingReceipt (3 fields), and OFTReceipt (2 fields). These 4 structs are defined twice, totaling ~56 lines of pure duplication. Any change to these types must be synchronized between both interfaces.

findings.title: Repeated storage reads of _chainCredits[eid] in CreditManager functions
findings.description: In sendCredits (L100-120), _chainCredits[dstEid] is accessed 4 times as separate SLOAD operations. In restoreCredit (L128-136), _chainCredits[eid] is accessed 3 times. In _reduceCredit (L301-313), _chainCredits[eid] is accessed 5 times. Caching the storage pointer as a local variable would clarify intent and may save gas on repeated slot lookups.

findings.title: Magic number 10000 used directly in LiquidityPool and PPTSatellite instead of named constant
findings.description: LiquidityPool.utilizationRatio (L92) uses the literal 10000 for basis points denomination. PPTSatellite.previewInstantWithdraw (L135) and instantWithdraw (L218) also use literal 10000. Meanwhile, CreditManager properly defines BPS_DENOMINATOR = 10000 as a named constant. Inconsistent use of magic numbers vs. named constants across the codebase.

findings.title: Duplicate quoteSend pattern between PPTOFT and PPTOFTAdapter with identical structure
findings.description: Both PPTOFT.quoteSend (L153-162) and PPTOFTAdapter.quoteSend (L160-169) have identical implementations with the same signature, same ternary for options fallback, same _buildSendMessage call, and same _quote delegation. This reinforces the need for a shared OFT base contract (related to finding simplify-003).

findings.title: Duplicate send function structure between PPTOFT and PPTOFTAdapter
findings.description: PPTOFT.send (L185-208) and PPTOFTAdapter.send (L179-202) share identical structure: validate amount, call _debitView, debit tokens (burn vs. safeTransferFrom), build message, send via LZ, emit OFTSent. The only difference is the debit mechanism (burn vs. lock). This is a classic Template Method pattern where the base provides the algorithm skeleton and subclasses override only the debit step.

findings.title: PPTSatellite.deposit and withdraw share common cross-chain send boilerplate
findings.description: PPTSatellite.deposit (L187-199) and PPTSatellite.withdraw (L251-263) share 7 identical lines of cross-chain send boilerplate: build options, quote fee, check msg.value, call _lzSend. The only difference is the payload construction. This pattern repeats within a single contract.

findings.title: Redundant explicit return in DeltaLib.calculateOptimalWeights
findings.description: calculateOptimalWeights uses a named return variable 'weights' but also has two explicit 'return weights' statements (L50 and L57). Since 'weights' is the named return, the function will automatically return it at the end. The early 'return weights' at L50 is fine for control flow (short-circuiting), but the final 'return weights' at L57 is redundant.

summary.verdict: The codebase has a clear pattern of code duplication stemming from two root causes: (1) Shared libraries LzOptionsLib and LayerZeroErrors were created but never imported by any contract, leaving 5+ copies of identical functions and error definitions. (2) PPTOFT and PPTOFTAdapter duplicate at least 5 functions that belong in a shared OFT base contract. The CreditManager.rebalance function is the highest-complexity hotspot with nested branching inside a loop. No individual function exceeds 50 lines, keeping all findings at P2-P3 severity. The primary recommendation is to actually use the existing shared libraries and extract a common OFTCore base contract.
